messages:
Maria (PM): Quick sync thread — after today's launch we need to lock down how we handle the next 2 weeks: concentrated bug-first push vs split team (bugs + a couple small UX enhancements). I sketched a lightweight proposal below, please react or reply. TL;DR: 5-day focused bug wave for P0/P1 + small parallel UX work (2 engineer-PM pairs, low-risk).

Sanjay: Can you post counts? how many P0/P1 we’re looking at now? link to query would help.

Olivia (Eng): From infra signals we’re seeing increased retry rates on /stream and a spike in connection resets. If we push enhancements first we risk more support churn.

Tom (Support): Current customer reports: 8 mentions of #login-flash (3 reproducible), 5 intermittent streaming complaints, 2 reports from Dedicated customers with high impact. I can surface exact ticket IDs in the 3pm sync.

Lee: If we go bugs-first do we freeze the polish rollouts? We could instead A/B the top enhancement to 10% to keep momentum and limit risk.

Maria (PM): Proposed decision criteria: severity (P0/P1), revenue/contract impact, frequency (user surface), rollback complexity, and cross-team dependencies. Proposed commit for this sprint: reserve ~40% dev capacity for bug remediation (P0/P1), allow up to 2 small enhancements (each 1–2 sprints) with low rollback risk. Daily triage, and a canary gate for any enhancement deploy.

Olivia (Eng): Agree with the split. Suggest we enforce labels so triage is fast: triage/bug-priority, triage/enhancement-candidate. Example query: `is:open label:triage/bug-priority created:>2026-03-01` — I'll add automation to tag new reports.

Sanjay: Also propose a quick regression harness run on canary before any enhancement rollout. I can wire up a job so deploy-bot runs `smoke-suite --canary` on PR merge. Saves us from blind rollouts.

deploy-bot: smoke tests queued on canary-2 for branch release/2026-03-19. Status: queued.

Maria (PM): Operational asks: @Tom please prioritize customer callbacks for top 5 affected customers and capture acceptance conditions they need. @Lee please estimate fix effort for the top P0s by EOD. We'll meet at 15:00 to finalize.

Tom (Support): I can own callbacks. ETA to customers: 48h for an initial update. I'll include a short survey to capture regression frequency. :phone:

Lee: Rough estimates coming now — 3 P0s look like ~2–3 engineer-days each (one may be a config roll). P1s are smaller. I'll update the issue backlog with estimates and mark any that need infra assistance.

Olivia (Eng): Note: Dedicated customers require isolated handling and SLA notices. If we reallocate engineers, keep one infra on-call for rollback and another for monitoring tweaks.

Maria (PM): Great. Next steps before 15:00 sync: 1) Lee posts estimates, 2) Tom starts callbacks, 3) Olivia wires tagging automation, 4) Sanjay wires the smoke job. I'll create the sprint slice and apply labels so engineering can pick up. Final decision in 15:00 meeting. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Sanjay: One more thing — if we do the 40% bug reserve and 2 enhancement tracks, let's gate enhancements by a short checklist (canary pass, customer-impact review, rollback plan). I can draft the checklist before the meeting.

Maria (PM): Perfect — bring the checklist to 15:00 and we'll sign off.
